name: Duncan Stahl
occupation: Former fishing worker and hotel cleaner
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember making a scar disappear into my hand's ordinary lines.” On Friday, near Breakwater Way, Duncan stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I agreed to show my nails. Nobody asked whether my accident was part of the product.
appearance: Duncan is easy to recognize by close-cropped dark curls and a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling. Usually dressed in a brown corduroy jacket with a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it, Duncan listens with the head tilted a little to the left when listening.
personality: Duncan has a long memory for unfair prices and a short one for small insults. Duncan can get along perfectly well with an enemy provided the account between them is clear.
agenda: To approve the uses of the scarred hand separately.
family: Vivian Acosta is Duncan’s half-sibling. Duncan is free to hang up first. Vivian makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *Station steps in rain*, Vivian says, “I came to complain about my street and held an umbrella over the officer I was going to name.”
connections: Ruth Sutton. The model and the photographer agree which parts of the hand's history are for sale. Also in the story is Casey Hunter (former crewmate).

reactions.situation: A campaign manager wants to enlarge the scar
reactions.response: Duncan asks the model whether the original permission covers the scar.

reactions.situation: A witness is embarrassed about remembering only a little
reactions.response: Duncan asks where they stood and what they could hear, leaving the rest open instead of filling it with guesses.
